title: How Many Parts an Hour: Cycle Time Built From Its Pieces, the Speed Override It Takes to Hit a Target, and What a Person Standing Near Costs

artifact.note: the cycle time of a pick and place as a sum of its pieces: the moves (each a trapezoid of distance, speed and acceleration, with the slow approach to a contact and the speed cap from a person's nearness), the hand's closing and opening, and the settling; the throughput from it; the speed override that a target cycle time needs (found by bisection, since the contact speed does not scale); and the cycle time with a person at a given distance, from the speed limit of the separation lesson
